evidence_tree.built_with: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>
evidence_tree.scope_honored: Only data/ and docs/math-foundations.md were read. src/, tests/, scripts/, docs/plans/, docs/receipts/, the diff, and git history were NOT read.
evidence_tree.limitation: The scenario definition for 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' (roster composition, champion list, item assignment, fight window) does NOT exist anywhere in the permitted export. grep for 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster', 'coupled_scenarios' and 'damage_taken' over the whole export returned zero hits. The computation below is therefore a structural reconstruction from the two golden values plus the cached wiki text, not a forward re-simulation of the fight.

sources_quoted.quote: After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).

... gain '''bonus''' [[health regeneration]] per second equal to {{as|{{rd|0 to 5 for 11|0 to 3.75 for 11|...}}|health}} for 8 seconds ... [[Area of effect]], [[damage over time]], or [[damage|proc]] damage taken trigger this effect with the {{tip|ranged}} values.
sources_quoted.why: Decisive, in-export proof of the {{rd|...}} argument order: the SECOND argument is the ranged branch (the sentence names 'the ranged values' for the lower 0-to-3.75 figure). Therefore {{rd|8%|5%}} = 8% melee / 5% ranged.

sources_quoted.locator: item 3181 (Hullbreaker) -> passives[1]; item 3748 (Titanic Hydra); item 6333 (Death's Dance)
sources_quoted.quote: Hullbreaker: {{rd|120%|{{ap|120*0.7}}%}} '''base''' AD ... {{rd|5%|{{ap|5*0.7}}%}} '''maximum''' health   |   Titanic Hydra: {{rd|1%|{{fd|0.5}}%}} '''maximum''' health   |   Death's Dance: Reduces {{rd|30%|10%}} of all post-mitigation ... damage received
sources_quoted.why: Corroborates the melee-first/ranged-second order across the cache: the second argument is systematically the reduced (x0.7, x0.5) ranged branch. The {{rd}} split is keyed on the ITEM HOLDER's melee/ranged classification, never on the target's - no item in the cache varies a number by the target's range class.

sources_quoted.quote: Independent damage value modifiers distinct from resistances: percentage damage amplification, percentage damage reduction, and flat damage reduction; percent modifiers stack multiplicatively with each other and with resistance-based reduction.
sources_quoted.why: Fixes Expose Weakness as a multiplicative post-mitigation amplifier applied on top of the 100/(100+R) mitigation, i.e. damage_taken = (1 + amp) x post_mitigation over the amplified window.

sources_quoted.quote: m(R) = 100 / (100 + R)          (apply_resistance, resistance.py)  ...  post = raw . m(R)
sources_quoted.why: Mitigation is a per-instance multiplier independent of the Bloodsong amp, so swapping only the amp rate rescales exactly the amplified window and leaves the rest of damage_taken untouched - which is what lets the two golden totals be decomposed linearly below.

sources_quoted.quote: Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks.
sources_quoted.why: The other item named by the scenario. Carve carries no melee/ranged split and no 8%/5% pair; it cannot produce the observed delta shape (see rejected hypothesis H3).

sources_quoted.quote: atoms: stats.health {flat: 200.0}, stats.gold-per-10 {flat: 9.0}, damage.on-hit (behavior Spellblade), damage.on-attack (behavior Spellblade), ... (no parameterised amplifier atom)
sources_quoted.why: Confirms the Expose Weakness amplifier percentage is carried ONLY by the wiki branch text S1 - there is no competing numeric source for it in the cache, so 8% and 5% are the only two admissible values.

step_1_identify_the_moved_quantity.search: The only melee/ranged pair equal to (8%, 5%) anywhere in data/items.json is Bloodsong's Expose Weakness (S1). The scenario name names Bloodsong. Expose Weakness is the only cached effect that raises a participant's damage_taken as a target-side amplifier.

step_2_solve_the_two_golden_totals_as_on.model: damage_taken = U + (1 + a) * B, where B = post-mitigation damage landing inside the 4 s Expose Weakness window and U = post-mitigation damage outside it (S4, S5: the amp is a multiplicative modifier on top of 100/(100+R)).
step_2_solve_the_two_golden_totals_as_on.sanity: U and B are both positive and B/(U+B) = 1100.0/3986.9 = 27.6% of the fight's pre-amp damage falls inside the amplified window - consistent with S1's 4 s debuff duration and 1.5 s re-application cooldown inside a longer coupled fight. The amp is therefore correctly windowed, not applied to the whole fight: 4074.9/1.08*1.05 = 3961.71 != 4041.9, so a whole-fight amp is ruled out.

step_3_rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: The amp rate stayed 8% and the amplified window B shrank (a windowing fix rather than a rate fix).
step_3_rejected_hypotheses.test: Requires delta B = 33.0/0.08 = 412.5. Arithmetically possible but has no support in the cache: it predicts no relationship between the two golden values and the pair (8%, 5%), whereas the observed pair reproduces BOTH totals exactly from one shared (U, B). Rejected as strictly less explanatory.

step_3_rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: The amp composition changed from multiplicative to additive with another amplifier a2.
step_3_rejected_hypotheses.test: delta = 0.08 * a2 * B = 33.0 requires B = 412.5/a2. For any a2 <= 0.10 this gives B >= 4125, which already exceeds the total post-amp damage_taken of 4074.9 before adding U and the second amp. Arithmetically impossible.

step_3_rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: Black Cleaver's average-stack model changed (docs/math-foundations.md Section 2.3 item 2, the 0.8*max_stacks constant vs the Cesaro mean C - C(C-1)/(2h)).
step_3_rejected_hypotheses.test: Carve (S6) is 6% armor reduction per stack with no melee/ranged split, so it cannot generate an 8%/5% pair. Under a pure mitigation change the ratio (100+R_old)/(100+R_new) = 4074.9/4041.9 = 1.008165 forces, for an all-physical single-source target, an armor of ~15 - implausible for a roster participant absorbing ~4 k damage, and inconsistent with a mixed-source roster. Section 2.3 also flags the Cesaro replacement as a P3 candidate explicitly out of scope for the foundations work, and notes it 'changing it re-tunes every BC fight in the corpus' - i.e. it would not surface as a single isolated leaf shift.

step_3_rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: Both values wrong (some third amp rate).
step_3_rejected_hypotheses.test: S1 admits exactly two legal values for Expose Weakness, 8% and 5%, and the two golden totals are exactly the two solutions of the same (U, B) decomposition at those two rates. No third rate is sourced anywhere in the cache (S7).

step_4_which_branch_is_correct.rule_established: From S2 (decisive) plus S3 (corroborating): {{rd|X|Y}} = X for a MELEE holder, Y for a RANGED holder, keyed on the item HOLDER, not the target. So Bloodsong's Expose Weakness = +8% damage taken when the Bloodsong holder is melee, +5% when the holder is ranged.
step_4_which_branch_is_correct.resolution: The correct leaf value is 4074.9 if the Bloodsong holder in this roster is melee, and 4041.9 if the holder is ranged. The roster is not in the permitted evidence tree, so the holder's range class was resolved by inference rather than by direct lookup:
inference: (a) The default single-value read of '{{rd|8%|5%}}' - the failure mode of any accessor that does not model the melee/ranged split - yields the FIRST argument, 8%. The OLD value is exactly that default.
(b) Producing 5% requires the melee/ranged branch to exist and to have been evaluated. The change therefore added (or corrected) range-awareness; it is not a value that a range-blind reader can emit.

(c) A regression producing 5% would require the branch to already exist AND to be wired backwards (reading 'rd' as ranged-first). That is a strictly more elaborate failure than the range-blind first-argument default it would have to have replaced, and it would move melee-holder leaves too. Occam favours the fix.
(d) Under the fix reading, only ranged-holder scenarios move; this leaf moving DOWN to the second branch is exactly the expected signature.
step_4_which_branch_is_correct.residual_uncertainty: This conclusion is conditional on the Bloodsong holder in 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' being a RANGED champion. That fact could not be verified from data/ or docs/math-foundations.md. If the holder is melee, the correct value is 4074.9 (old) and the new value is a melee/ranged inversion. Recommended cheap confirmation for the parent: read the scenario's roster and confirm the Bloodsong holder's attack range class; the sourced rule (S2/S3) then decides the leaf with no further modelling.

conclusion: Bloodsong's Expose Weakness is a multiplicative, target-side damage amplifier of {{rd|8%|5%}} = 8% (melee holder) / 5% (ranged holder), applied over a 4 s window. Both golden values are exactly reproduced by one decomposition, U = 2886.9 unamplified + B = 1100.0 amplified, evaluated at 8% (old) and 5% (new). 5% is the ranged branch and is the value a range-aware accessor emits; 8% is the value a range-blind accessor emits by taking the first {{rd}} argument. The new value is the correct one for a ranged Bloodsong holder.
